RFC4659-3.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor). SHIFTED by 6e063fb498 (tests: give ten assert-nothing tests a real assertion), whose hunks sit in untagged sibling tests and the import block. The tagged unit is byte-identical (gate-verified) and no helper it calls changed. Verdict stands. Re-judged 2026-10-02 (BGP c34 judge). Both operator entry points that originate an IPv6 VPN route are proven. API: plugins/cmd/update/rfc4659_vpnv6_label_test.go, ParseUpdateText ipv6/mpls-vpn rd 65000:100 label 1000 yields the NLRI literal 88 003E81 0000FDE800000064 20010DB80001 (judge checked 1000<<4|BoS = 0x3E81, 136 bits) (positive); no label is refused with route.ErrMissingLabel and a nil result (negative). Config: bgp/config/rfc4659_vpnv6_label_test.go, YANG parse + PeersFromConfigTree keeps Labels [1000] on the VPN static route (positive; its wire form is asserted by the RFC4659-3.4-1 send unit, label 003e81 in MP_REACH), and a labelless configured route is refused at load with "requires at least one label" (negative). Records: parseVPNNLRI and patchStaticRoutes reverts, all four observed red; author probes dropping each label check red only the matching negative (scratch c34p/4659-a, 4659-b). message.BuildVPN still writes a labelless NLRI for empty Labels, but every shipped caller is guarded; its other caller is internal/chaos test tooling. HEAD vpn_test units stay as unrecorded supplementary tags. Rejudged 2026-10-17 (independent reader, not the author of 3f6bb1965e) after the owner-approved command-text change in 3f6bb1965e (injection grammar: nlri <family> became mp <family> for MP families and bare nlri for IPv4 unicast): both cmd/update units changed only the section keyword of their ParseUpdateText argument (nlri ipv6/mpls-vpn became mp ipv6/mpls-vpn); the positive still asserts the exact labeled NLRI 88 003E81 0000FDE800000064 20010DB80001 and the negative still requires route.ErrMissingLabel and a nil result, so each still fails if the label is dropped or the refusal goes. Package re-run green 2026-10-17. RFC 4659 Section 3.2: "When distributing IPv6 VPN routes, the advertising PE router MUST assign and distribute MPLS labels with the IPv6 VPN routes." The two records on these units are re-recorded in the same change. Verdict stands.

RFC4659-3.2-2.note: Forbidden: MP_REACH for a VPNv6 route with AFI != 2 or SAFI != 128. internal/component/bgp/message/update_build_test.go::TestUpdateBuilder_BuildVPN_IPv6: afi != 2 and value[2] != 128 are Errorf. Single-polarity marker.

RFC4659-3.2.1.1-1.note: Independently rejudged the full widened RFC 4659 Section 3.2.1.1 obligation. TestRFC4659ConfiguredIPv6TransportNextHopWire in internal/component/bgp/reactor/rfc4659_configured_ipv6_transport_integration_linux_test.go closes the former originator-identity proof gap: native configuration starts the real Peer and recipient Session over TCP6, with self and explicit selection under both grouping modes. Independent interface enumeration in separate namespaces establishes speaker ownership; the accepted endpoint supplies the self oracle and a distinct speaker-owned loopback supplies the explicit oracle. Literal recipient assertions require AFI 2/SAFI 128, length 24, every RD byte zero, the independently established speaker global address, both intended VPN NLRIs and completion at VPNv6 EOR. buildMPReachVPN is reached through configured static sending rather than called by the integration test. The earlier builder test remains an encoding control, and TestRFC4659LinkLocalPeeringPreservesUnspecifiedGlobalPair remains contextual exception evidence. Section 3.2.1 leaves transport-policy definition to the operator; this tests its existing configured control-plane expression, not tunnel creation. Distinct /128s exclude the separate common-subnet/48-octet origination obligation. IPv4-mapped transport, PE dataplane and ASBR gaps remain unchanged. Rejudged 2026-10-16 (independent reader) after the owner-approved 2026-10-16 change ("5 RFC") to TestRFC4659LinkLocalPeeringPreservesUnspecifiedGlobalPair: the one edit is in the forbidden-next-hop branch, where for the VPN (non-unicast) cases the expected MP_UNREACH_NLRI value now has its Compatibility octets want[4:7] (after AFI, SAFI and NLRI length 0x98) set to 80 00 00 in place of the received label octets 00 01 01. RFC 8277 Section 2.4: "Upon transmission, the Compatibility field SHOULD be set to 0x800000. Upon reception, the value of the Compatibility field MUST be ignored." The withdrawal still names the same RD and prefix and still requires no MP_REACH. This unit is contextual positive evidence for this single-polarity row, carried by the valid "link-local-only" case, whose exact 48-octet zero-RD unspecified-global plus zero-RD link-local MP_REACH assertion is byte-identical; the edit touches only the refused cases. Weight unchanged: the configured-transport integration test remains the main evidence. RFC 4659 Section 3.2.1.1: "the BGP speaker SHALL advertise a Next Hop Network Address field containing a VPN-IPv6 address - whose 8-octet RD is set to zero, and - whose 16-octet IPv6 address is set to the global IPv6 address of the advertising BGP speaker." Verdict stands. Rejudged 2026-10-16 (independent reader) after a comment-only edit to TestRFC4659LinkLocalPeeringPreservesUnspecifiedGlobalPair: the comment above the Compatibility substitution now reads "in place of the route's label octets 000101." (correcting "label 010100"); no input byte, expectation or assertion changed, so the judgement above stands. The unit's discrimination record was re-recorded the same day (revert of forward_next_hop.go::egressNextHopWithheld, observed red). Verdict stands.

RFC4659-3.2.1.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after 2a5ac0ce0b). RFC 4659 Section 3.2.1.1: "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if and only if the advertising BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the peer the route is being advertised to [BGP-IPv6]." and "In all other cases, a BGP speaker shall advertise to its peer in the Next Hop Network Address field only the global IPv6 address of the next hop." Since 990744517c (owner decision 2026-10-19, rfc-gap-difficulty-2026-10-18 #22) linkLocalConditionFor gives AFI 2/SAFI 128 the peer-only condition and every other family RFC 2545 Section 3's joint one; linkScope.holdsCommonSubnet answers it from peerOnLink and linkLocalNextHop still requires a speaker-owned global and a configured link-local. Paths traced: (1) configured: sendStaticRoutes/Grouped/withdraw pass route.Family() to linkLocalNextHopFor, buildStaticRouteUpdateNew -> vpnNextHopOctets/buildMPReachVPN write 24 or 48 with zero RDs, then the session gate re-applies the decision; (2) API: AnnounceNLRIBatch -> exportFilterForBody -> normalizeOrdinaryNextHop routes 24/48-octet SAFI 128 fields to normalizeVPNNextHop -> applyEgressNextHopScope(fam); (3) relayed: both forwarding rails call applyEgressNextHopScope, which raises a zero-RD 24-octet field for a speaker-owned global on the peer's subnet and trims a 48-octet pair only off it (link-local-only unspecified-global exception kept); (4) next-hop self and (5) explicit: applyLinkLocalNextHop decides the VPN pair on linkLocalConditionPeer independently of nhMode, vpnIPv6NextHop slices nhVPNPair[:48] or [:24]; (6) default route: sendDefaultOriginateRoutes always calls BuildUnicast with SAFI unset, so it emits no VPN-IPv6 route and this requirement has no default-route path (a VPN family passes the peer-only condition into a plain IPv6 body, but exportFilterForBody -> normalizeOrdinaryNextHop trims the 32-octet form on RFC 2545's joint condition). Peer.SendAnnounce has no non-test caller. Tagged units: TestRFC4659VPNv6LinkLocalLoopbackGlobal (new: loopback global off the shared /64, 48 octets on configured, relay, next-hop-self; 24 off-link), TestRFC4659StaticVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659APIVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659ForwardVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659ForwardVPNv6NextHopRewriteCarriesRD, test/encode/rfc4659-vpnv6-link-local-off-subnet.ci (now the 48-octet positive with the 24-octet form rejected); each asserts the exact field. Discrimination records (rfc/discrimination/rfc4659.json) are whole-body panics re-recorded by 990744517c; the checkVPNFRR tags carry none (two producers). Auditor overlay mutants (tags ze_core ze_bgp, go test -overlay), all killed: old joint rule for VPN (loopback test configured/relay/next-hop-self red, plus untagged RFC2545ReceivedPairSubnetConditions/vpn/global-off-link); never-48 (static, API, forward, rewrite, loopback tagged tests red); always-48 regardless of subnet (static, API, forward, rewrite, loopback off-link red); and the contrast mutant giving plain IPv6 the peer-only condition (RFC2545 unicast/global-off-link and second-address tests red). Baseline green. The RFC 2545 contrast is correct per its own text, Section 3: "if and only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to" (not judged here). Interop: 2a5ac0ce0b's checkVPNFRR positive (BIRD 2.15.1 holds Ze global plus link-local, both RDs zero) is a genuine independent receiver; its negative is NOT this requirement's negative: BIRD and FRR share the lab /64 with Ze, so the omitted link-local there is the speaker-owned/third-party gate, a neighbouring rule (RFC 2545 third-party gap), not "no common subnet". Residuals, not defects under the owner's reading: a third-party global sent to an on-link peer leaves without the speaker's link-local, which the iff's inclusion clause read alone would demand; Section 3.2.1.1 describes the global as "the global IPv6 address of the advertising BGP speaker", so the section does not contemplate it and the owner's #22 decision covers only the speaker's own global (open owner question). The .ci and the interop scenario were not re-run by this auditor. The encode fixture's common subnet is ::1/128.

RFC4659-3.4-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-14 (independent auditor). Only TestOpenAdvertisesVPNv6Capability changed, mechanically: it now packs ps.Capabilities through capability.PackOptionalParams (the one packer buildOpen uses) instead of the removed buildOptionalParams, then requires Multiprotocol AFI 2/SAFI 128 in the decoded OPEN parameters for a configured ipv6/mpls-vpn family. The send and receive units in rfc4659_vpnv6_negotiated_send_test.go (route sent only when AFI 2/SAFI 128 negotiated, UPDATE refused when not) and the negotiateWith negative are unchanged and still carry the enforcement.

RFC4659-8-5.note: Re-judged 2026-10-20 (independent auditor, authored none of the change). RFC 4659 Section 8: "When the VPN-IPv6 traffic is to be transported using IPv6 tunneling, the BGP Next Hop Field SHALL contain an IPv6 address." The only moved producer is sysrib.go::processEvent (41e11adf5c, OSPF unnumbered backup next hop): it copies BackupInterface/BackupOnLink into protocolRoute and nothing else. The non-CIDR branch is unchanged: a change whose Prefix is invalid but carries NLRI (VPN, EVPN, ...) is skipped with no FIB entry. buildMPReachVPN, checkRouteBestChange and mpReachNextHopHandler are unchanged since the last judgement. No ASBR-local label binding or tunnel-transport-driven next-hop decision exists. {gap} annotation still accurate; gap stands.
